why: Every post-snapshot Nakai result proves the conjecture for a restricted class of isolated hypersurface singularities (Brieskorn, fewnomial/cusp, modality ≤ 2, homogeneous, weighted homogeneous), so each is a case that confirms it. The two journal papers are digested by journal acceptance. The preprints are unreviewed, and so is the talk, which has no written argument and is doubtful. The OpenAI family 048 entries claim a counterexample to Lipman–Zariski, a different conjecture. The manuscript, which the second entry read, never addresses rings of differential operators or Nakai's hypothesis. Nakai ⇒ Lipman–Zariski would make a Lipman–Zariski counterexample a Nakai counterexample by contraposition, but that implication is known only from secondary summaries whose setting is unconfirmed. So I score those entries as variant: the model generated them, and they settle no part of the Nakai question on the record. Brumatti et al. is a variant because it concerns non-finite-type rings, and Singh's bounded-order reformulation is a variant too. The Yau–Zhu–Zuo derivation is an internal tool, not an object the statement asks for, so its object_role is null.
doubts: The two OpenAI entries describe one release of one manuscript and are duplicates. If Nakai ⇒ Lipman–Zariski holds unconditionally for complex affine varieties (Becker; Rego), a correct family 048 surface would refute Nakai outright, and the scope would become whole/refuted (unreviewed). The record could not confirm the hypotheses of that implication. The Annali date conflicts with the authors' list ('to appear, 2026'), but both dates fall after the snapshot. The Xiao–Yau–Zuo event has only a year (2025), which still falls after the snapshot.
